blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a 2004 paper by Nancy Leveson that analyzes five major spacecraft accidents (1996-2000) to extract systemic lessons applicable to modern systems like autonomous vehicles. The paper reveals striking similarities across accidents in three areas: safety culture (complacency, overconfidence, and resource prioritization), management/organizational flaws (diffusion of responsibility, poor communication), and technical deficiencies (inadequate engineering practices). Leveson argues that safety cannot be retrofitted via QA alone and requires dedicated system engineering focus. The author notes parallels to machine learning systems and emphasizes the need for better modeling tools to handle increasing system complexity. Key insights include the prevalence of design errors over implementation bugs and the critical role of documenting design rationale.
paper_title: The role of software in spacecraft accidents
paper_venue: AIAA Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets
